category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title = 'When the child uses 35 LOONIES for $35 — repairing the all-coins trap at Grade 2'. Trap is concrete and recovery_moves list 3 actions, but no named research is cited and recovery_moves do NOT branch by what the diagnostic told you about the child — they are a flat list (compare 35 loonies vs $20+$10+$5; drill biggest bill first; time the count).
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite the research grounding (e.g., NCTM Principles to Actions on equivalent representations, or CGI/Carpenter on part-whole composition with money) in the rationale, AND restructure recovery_moves to BRANCH by diagnostic: 'IF child can name a $20 bill on its own → drill biggest-bill-first decomposition; IF child cannot identify bill values → drop back to bill-recognition matching before reintroducing the mix; IF child mixes but loses track of total → use a running-sum number line on the record strip.'

category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials lists 'Coin + Bill Cards (1 set per pair)', 'Item Price Cards (20)', 'Lesson 3 formative tracker'. Puppets are explicitly OPTIONAL and time is 12/25/13 = 50 min, which is fine for Grade 2 — but the differentiation block ('for_emerging: Find 1 way only.', 'for_movement_learners: Walk between bill stations.') does NOT include a no-paper, no-purchase alternative path that uses only voice, body, or gesture for days when prep wasn't possible.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a no-materials variant inside differentiation, e.g.: 'No-paper version — children use FINGERS as bills (whole hand = $20 bill, one finger = $5; thumb = $10) and call out totals as a partner verifies by skip-counting aloud. Body becomes the wallet — works on any day with zero prep.' Make sure this variant still hits the same success criteria (mix bills + coins, find 3 ways, verify totals).

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.common_misconceptions = ['Coins always = simpler. (Repair: bills for big amounts.)', 'Bills only for $50+. (Repair: any big amount.)']. The conceptual progression on equivalence is clean and manipulatives carry meaning, but the lesson does NOT explicitly let children INVENT or REFINE a strategy and COMPARE strategies, and the misconception is not named in research-grounded terms (no reference to part-whole composition, additive composition, or named work like Carpenter & Moser CGI part-part-whole, Fuson on multi-unit numeration, or NCTM equivalent-representations literature).
category_feedback.required_fix: In consolidation.discussion_prompts, add an explicit strategy-comparison move: 'Two pairs share their $35 combos. Which used FEWER pieces? Which started with the BIGGEST bill? Which counted-on from a bill? Are both valid? Why?' Then in expanded_walkthrough.rationale, name the misconception in research-grounded terms (e.g., 'This is a part-whole composition gap — Carpenter & Moser; children treat money as a unitary count rather than as composed values') so a substitute teacher knows the conceptual lever.

grader_notes: Pair 3 is close — alignment, voice, and lesson-worksheet consistency all clear at 4. The three blocking 3s all sit in the LESSON (not the worksheet): the trap recovery doesn't branch by diagnostic, there's no no-materials alternative path, and the math-authenticity bar wants children to compare strategies AND a research-grounded name for the misconception. Worksheet Part 3 (fewest pieces) is a strong transfer task — keep it. Fixes are surgical edits to expanded_walkthrough, differentiation, and consolidation.discussion_prompts in lesson_03 only.
